::: {.route-question}
Question for today: CellCo's coating machine wears out. When should it be maintained, and what does the right policy save?
:::

## From a chain to a decision {#mdp}

::: {.two}
::: {}
A **Markov decision process** adds choices to a Markov chain. In each state the planner picks an **action**, which sets both the cost and the transition probabilities.

A **policy** names one action for every state. Each policy is an ordinary Markov chain, so its steady state gives its long-run cost per shift.
:::
::: {}
```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>State</th><th>If continued: next state (G, Mi, Ma, F)</th><th class="num">Cost, CNY</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>Good (G)</td><td>0.80, 0.15, 0.04, 0.01</td><td class="num">0</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Minor wear (Mi)</td><td>0, 0.85, 0.12, 0.03</td><td class="num">500</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Major wear (Ma)</td><td>0, 0, 0.60, 0.40</td><td class="num">3,000</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Failed (F)</td><td>repair to Good</td><td class="num">20,000</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```
[In Minor or Major wear, preventive maintenance (PM) restores Good before the next shift for CNY 6,000.]{.hint}
:::
:::

## Four policies, four costs {#policies}

```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Policy (action in Minor, in Major)</th><th class="num">Steady state G, Mi, Ma, F</th><th class="num">Cost per shift, CNY</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>Run to failure (continue, continue)</td><td class="num">0.385, 0.385, 0.154, 0.077</td><td class="num">2,192</td></tr>
    <tr><td>PM in Minor only (PM, continue)</td><td class="num">0.769, 0.115, 0.077, 0.038</td><td class="num">1,692</td></tr>
    <tr><td>PM at any wear (PM, PM)</td><td class="num">0.833, 0.125, 0.033, 0.008</td><td class="num">1,117</td></tr>
    <tr><td>PM in Major only (continue, PM)</td><td class="num">0.455, 0.455, 0.073, 0.018</td><td class="num hit">1,027</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

::: {.bridge}
Cost per shift = Σ π~i~ × cost of the chosen action in state i. Maintaining only at major wear is cheapest, **53% below** running to failure, and 8% below maintaining at any sign of wear.
:::

## Try a policy {#mdp-explorer data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="widget" id="mdx">
  <div class="w-controls">
    <span>In Minor wear:</span><span class="w-toggle" data-s="1"><button type="button" data-a="C" aria-pressed="true">Continue</button><button type="button" data-a="PM" aria-pressed="false">PM</button></span>
    <span>In Major wear:</span><span class="w-toggle" data-s="2"><button type="button" data-a="C" aria-pressed="true">Continue</button><button type="button" data-a="PM" aria-pressed="false">PM</button></span>
    <label class="w-slider">PM cost, CNY <strong id="mdx-pm-v">6,000</strong><input type="range" id="mdx-pm" min="1000" max="30000" step="500" value="6000"></label>
  </div>
  <table class="wide" id="mdx-t"></table>
  <div class="w-readout" id="mdx-out" aria-live="polite"></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('mdx'); if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  const PC = [[0.80, 0.15, 0.04, 0.01], [0, 0.85, 0.12, 0.03], [0, 0, 0.60, 0.40], [1, 0, 0, 0]], CC = [0, 500, 3000, 20000];
  const pol = ['C', 'C', 'C', 'C'];
  function steady(P) {
    // power iteration on the chain
    let v = [0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25];
    for (let k = 0; k < 2000; k++) v = [0, 1, 2, 3].map((j) => v.reduce((s, x, i) => s + x * P[i][j], 0));
    return v;
  }
  function cost(a1, a2, pm) {
    const acts = ['C', a1, a2, 'C'];
    const P = PC.map((r, i) => (acts[i] === 'PM' ? [1, 0, 0, 0] : r)), c = CC.map((x, i) => (acts[i] === 'PM' ? pm : x));
    const pi = steady(P); return [pi, pi.reduce((s, x, i) => s + x * c[i], 0)];
  }
  const fmt = (x) => Math.round(x).toLocaleString('en-US');
  function draw() {
    const pm = +document.getElementById('mdx-pm').value; document.getElementById('mdx-pm-v').textContent = fmt(pm);
    const all = [['C', 'C', 'Run to failure'], ['PM', 'C', 'PM in Minor only'], ['PM', 'PM', 'PM at any wear'], ['C', 'PM', 'PM in Major only']].map(([a, b, n]) => [a, b, n, ...cost(a, b, pm)]);
    const best = all.reduce((m, x) => (x[4] < m[4] ? x : m));
    const mine = all.find((x) => x[0] === pol[1] && x[1] === pol[2]);
    document.getElementById('mdx-t').innerHTML = '<thead><tr><th>Policy</th><th class="num">Steady state G, Mi, Ma, F</th><th class="num">Cost per shift, CNY</th></tr></thead><tbody>' +
      all.map((x) => `<tr><td>${x[2]}${x === mine ? ' (yours)' : ''}</td><td class="num">${x[3].map((p) => p.toFixed(3)).join(', ')}</td><td class="num${x === best ? ' hit' : ''}">${fmt(x[4])}</td></tr>`).join('') + '</tbody>';
    document.getElementById('mdx-out').innerHTML = `Your policy costs <b>CNY ${fmt(mine[4])}</b> per shift. Best at this PM cost: <span class="best">${best[2]}, CNY ${fmt(best[4])}</span>` +
      (mine === best ? '. You found it.' : `, which saves CNY ${fmt(mine[4] - best[4])} per shift.`);
  }
  root.querySelectorAll('.w-toggle[data-s]').forEach((g) => g.querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.addEventListener('click', () => {
    pol[+g.dataset.s] = b.dataset.a; g.querySelectorAll('button').forEach((x) => x.setAttribute('aria-pressed', x === b)); draw(); })));
  document.getElementById('mdx-pm').addEventListener('input', draw);
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

## Activity · Answer {#act1-answer}

::: {.two}
::: {}
```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>PM cost, CNY</th><th>Best policy</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>below 4,960</td><td>PM at any wear</td></tr>
    <tr><td>4,960 to 22,020</td><td class="hit">PM in Major only</td></tr>
    <tr><td>above 22,020</td><td>Run to failure</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```
:::
::: {}
At today's CNY 6,000, PM in Major only is best, but the margin over PM at any wear is only CNY 90 per shift.

The number to track is the PM cost relative to the cost of a failure. If a PM contract falls below about CNY 5,000, the policy should change.
:::
:::

## Policy iteration {#policy-iteration}

::: {.two}
::: {}
1. **Evaluate** the current policy: solve g + h~i~ = c~i~ + Σ~j~ p~ij~ h~j~ with h~G~ = 0. Here g is the cost per shift and h~i~ the extra cost of starting in state i.
2. **Improve**: in each state, pick the action with the smallest c + Σ p h.
3. Repeat until no action changes.
:::
::: {}
```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Iteration</th><th>Policy (Minor, Major)</th><th class="num">g, CNY/shift</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>0</td><td>continue, continue</td><td class="num">2,192</td></tr>
    <tr><td>1</td><td>PM, PM</td><td class="num">1,117</td></tr>
    <tr><td>2</td><td>continue, PM</td><td class="num hit">1,027</td></tr>
    <tr><td>3</td><td>no change: optimal</td><td class="num">1,027</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```
:::
:::

[With four policies we can list them all. A real plant with ten wear levels and three actions has 3^10^ = 59,049 policies; policy iteration still finds the best in a few steps.]{.note-line}

## What we learned {#debrief}

::: {.takeaways}
::: {.tk}
An MDP is a Markov chain whose transitions and costs depend on the action chosen in each state. Every policy has a steady state and a cost per shift.
:::
::: {.tk}
For CellCo's coating machine, PM only at major wear costs CNY 1,027 per shift, 53% less than running to failure.
:::
::: {.tk .key}
The best policy depends on prices. Below a PM cost of about CNY 5,000, maintaining at any wear becomes best.
:::
:::
